--- title: "[StepUnknown]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Recode missing categorical levels to an explicit ``"unknown"`` level. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_unknown.py#L117-L247){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepUnknown(columns, new_level=DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_LEVEL, id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each selected categorical column has its nulls replaced in place by ``new_level``. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to recode. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.nominal_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.string()``, ``polars.selectors.string()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only categorical columns are meaningful here. [new_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_LEVEL
]{.doc-parameter-default} : The level that replaces nulls. Default ``"unknown"``. A `UserWarning` is emitted if a selected column already contains this level, since the recoded rows then become indistinguishable from real ones. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"unknown"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Nulls in the selected column are recoded in place to an explicit ``"unknown"`` level: ::: {#0ed15abe .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame( {"city": pd.Series(["NYC", "LA", "NYC", None], dtype="category")} ) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
city
0 NYC
1 LA
2 NYC
3 NaN
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#1214f3d3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepUnknown(s.nominal_predictors())) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_unknown(select(role='predictor', type=(String, Categorical, Enum))) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` records the level to add to each column: ::: {#bb2e9ad5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 1 columns — 1 predictor Steps: step_unknown(city) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` recodes the nulls in place: ::: {#cd388fa8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
city
0 NYC
1 LA
2 NYC
3 unknown
``` ::: ::: ``new_level`` names the added level: ::: {#724ee0a3 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepUnknown(s.nominal_predictors(), new_level="missing")) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
city
0 NYC
1 LA
2 NYC
3 missing
``` ::: :::
